source.publication: 2025 Form 80-100 Resident, Non-Resident and Part-Year Resident Individual Income Tax Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and the 2025 Form 80-105 Resident Return (Rev. 09/25)
source.section: Form 80-105 page 1 lines 8-17 and page 2 lines 38-66; Instructions PDF p.5 Filing Status and Exemptions table; p.6 Additional Exemptions, Lines 8-12; p.7 Lines 14-17; p.22 Tax Rates; p.27 Schedule of Tax Computation lines 1-4; Instructions PDF p.11 Line 46; FAQ 'Is Social Security taxable in Mississippi?'

worked: Federal AGI = wages (person 0) 50,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 = 75,500.00. Social Security received 30,000.00, of which 25,500.00 is taxable federally (given). Federal taxable income = 75,500.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 additional = 57,750.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form 80-105 filing status box 5, Single. Start at federal AGI 75,500.00 (Mississippi builds its own income on lines 38 to 66; the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt income, the same result here). Less Social Security 25,500.00 (Line 46: exempt in total; the form has no line for it). Line 66 and line 13 Mississippi AGI = 50,000.00. Line 14 standard deduction 2,300.00. Line 8 age boxes checked 1; line 10 = 1 x 1,500.00 = 1,500.00; line 11 6,000.00; line 12 and line 15 = 7,500.00. Line 16 Mississippi taxable income = 50,000.00 - 2,300.00 - 7,500.00 = 40,200.00. Schedule of Tax Computation line 1: first 10,000.00 x 0% = 0.00; line 2: remaining 30,200.00 x 4.4% = 1,328.80; line 4 and line 17 = 1,328.80. Lines 18 and 19 credits 0.00; line 20 = 1,328.80. The form rounds to whole dollars (p.22), which would give 1,329; expected keeps the formula result.
accepted_approximations: Mississippi builds its own income (Form 80-105 lines 38 to 66); the projection starts from federal AGI and removes the exempt income through the reliefs and Social Security treatment.
